primary_purpose: Connect Zahavy's abductive-jump question to an executable Missing Link before-image: the candidate generator, admission contract, and intervention verifier must be distinguishable before any capability claim can be evaluated.
claim_boundary: Configuration-contract reproduction only. No general LLM capability, biomedical discovery, paper-thesis, or world-model sufficiency claim is made.

api_summary.title: Operationalizing the abductive jump — Missing Link dogfood audit
api_summary.brief: A paper-to-code crosswalk for Zahavy's abductive-jump question: this fixture records no independent candidate jump, an incoherent admission contract, and no intervention verifier; it is not an LLM capability verdict.
api_summary.summary: TOE-TEST-0060 links Tom Zahavy's ICML 2026 position paper to an executable Missing Link characterization. The source snapshot produces 12 query restatements and accepts 0 candidates; its biomedical profile also assigns conflicting grounding and novelty constraints to the same overlap quantity. The result is ABSTAIN: the run exposes an incomplete proposal-to-verification contract, not a proof that LLMs cannot abduct or that world models are sufficient.
findings: The fixture has evidence input but does not observe an independently expressed abductive candidate: all 12 candidates are query restatements.
The admission layer is incoherent in the biomedical profile: max_single >= 0.92 and max_single <= 0.90.
No action-controllable world-model or intervention verifier is exercised by this run.
A future after-image must separately measure proposal novelty, evidence support, and an explicitly named intervention result.
